text:
kevin: heads up — seeing a p99 mem growth on prod llama-13b pools starting ~03:10 UTC. looks like KV page allocations steadily climb and never compact 
kevin: rough symptom: long-context sessions (8k+ prefix) eventually trigger a flurry of small page evicts+allocs, then we get sustained swap-like behaviour on the slab :/ 
kevin: stacktrace-ish from runtime metrics (snip):
```
pool=llama-13b-1   active_sessions=421  seq_dist=6k-14k
kv.pages_allocated: 12,048 -> 80,824 (03:10 -> 03:23)
kv.pages_free: 4,912 -> 2,100
evict_ops/sec: 18 -> 240
page_frag_ratio: 1.8 -> 3.6
kernel_mode: mqa_fallback (generic) selected after mismatch
```
kevin: also noticed routing fallback to qwen-7b for short answers during bursts; not sure if cross-model routing influences slab layout but it's timing-correlated

sasha: :eyes: thanks, Kevin. did this coincide with the 02:58 deploy? deploy-bot said rollout completed then.
sasha: do we have a pprof heap snapshot from a live worker?

kevin: yep i grabbed an allocation profile before and after the wave. attaching the trimmed output below:
```
-- before --
allocated_pages: 11800
largest_free_run: 640
-- after --
allocated_pages: 80400
largest_free_run: 32
notes: many small free fragments, high coalescing churn
```

maya: smell like fragmentation + repeated small writes into KV pages. long prefixes + rope scaling can push storage to new pages frequently. if kernel selection drops to the generic MQA path we do extra memcopy which amplifies churn.

maya: possible causes: rope scaling factor spike, kv_prefetch disabled for large requests, or batching heuristics producing tiny batches that align badly with page boundaries

jun: agree. also seen this when batching heuristics push many 1-2 token micro-batches during chat typing streams — each tiny batch may allocate a fresh tail page, then eviction triggers RC updates. combined with GQA->MQA model variant switch, kernel chooses slower path and allocator pressure spikes

kevin: reproduction plan i used: perf-harness script that replays 8k-prefix/4k-completion across 400 concurrent sessions for 15 mins. command:
```
./tools/perf/replay --model llama-13b --prefix-file testdata/8k_prefix.json --concurrency 400 --rate 80
```
kevin: that reproduces the steady climb locally in ~8 minutes

sasha: good repro. next steps: 1) bisect kernel selection change (recent mqa fallback heuristics), 2) enable kv_prefetch heuristics for long prefixes as an experiment, 3) run slab coalesce more aggressively as a mitigation

sasha: i'll start a bisect on the runtime branch now (range: f2b3c8..a9d2e1)

ops-bot: scheduling loadtest on staging cluster (staging-perf-03) — ETA 5m

deploy-bot: deploy f2b3c8 -> staging (job 43912) completed 03:42:12 UTC

jun: quick patch idea: bump kv_prefetch_threshold from 4096 -> 16384 for long-context pools, and enable larger batch coalescing windows (batch_coalesce_ms: 10 -> 25) for the experiment. should reduce tail page churn.

maya: note: increasing coalesce_ms will increase latency tail for interactive users. only ok as controlled experiment on long-context dedicated pools.

kevin: running a variant with kv_prefetch=16k + batch_coalesce=25ms now on a canary pool. will report back in 10m

sasha: bisect update: found candidate commit that changed MQA fallback heuristics (commit a7e9f4) — it moves to generic kernel when rope_scale > 1.2 and available_kvslots < 256. seems like a conservative choice but maybe noisy thresholds cause premature fallback

kevin: that commit matches the timeline. hypothesis: the fallback kicks in mid-session, kernel swaps, and allocator sees different write patterns -> fragmentation cascade

jun: if we revert the threshold tweak and instead add a gradual kernel transition (drain+warm pages) we can avoid abrupt layout changes. small patch idea: when moving to generic kernel, attempt to consolidate active KV pages into aligned runs before switching (max 50ms extra work)

maya: create a short lived workaround: revert the threshold change in prod for long-context pools and enable kv_prefetch 16k. if that stabilizes, we implement gradual kernel transition in runtime codepath.

kevin: can confirm canary with kv_prefetch=16k shows much lower evict_ops (18 -> 22) and fragmentation stays stable over 20m. will keep it running and prepare rollback if anything odd

sasha: assigning follow-ups: sasha -> bisect and revert plan, jun -> implement gradual kernel transition prototype, maya -> telemetry knobs + perf dashboard update, kevin -> monitor canary and paste pprof after 30m

kevin: ack. will paste final pprof snapshot 30m after canary start. for now :thumbsup:
